articles.standfirst: El club rojiblanco mantiene conversaciones con el entorno del centrocampista serbio del Almería, que tiene una cláusula de 40 millones y contrato hasta 2032
articles.summary: El club rojiblanco mantiene conversaciones con el entorno del centrocampista serbio del Almería, que tiene una cláusula de 40 millones y contrato hasta 2032
articles.body: El Atlético de Madrid ya trabaja en la planificación de la próxima temporada y uno de los nombres que ha aparecido en su agenda es el de Stefan Džodić. El centrocampista serbio de 21 años, actualmente en las filas del Almería, se ha convertido en uno de los objetivos de la dirección deportiva rojiblanca para reforzar su plantilla el próximo verano. Según ha podido saber MARCA, el Atlético mantiene conversaciones con el entorno del futbolista con la intención de sentar las bases de una posible operación. Todavía no existe un acuerdo cerrado, pero el interés es firme y en el Metropolitano consideran que Džodić reúne las condiciones necesarias para convertirse en una apuesta de futuro. La operación presenta algunas particularidades. El internacional serbio tiene contrato con el Almería hasta junio de 2032 y cuenta con una cláusula de rescisión de 40 millones de euros, una cantidad importante que marca el punto de partida de cualquier negociación. Sin embargo, las excelentes relaciones que mantienen ambas entidades podrían facilitar un entendimiento sin necesidad de alcanzar esa cifra. En los despachos del Atlético valoran especialmente el potencial de crecimiento del futbolista. A sus 21 años, Džodić es contemplado como un activo interesante tanto por su presente como por el margen de evolución que todavía tiene por delante. Su condición de internacional con Serbia también refuerza el atractivo de un jugador al que el club madrileño sigue de cerca. La intención rojiblanca es avanzar en los contactos durante los próximos meses para intentar encarrilar su incorporación de cara al mercado estival de 2027. El Almería, por su parte, cuenta con la protección de un contrato de larga duración y una cláusula elevada, por lo que no existe ninguna necesidad contractual de precipitar una salida. El Atlético ya ha comenzado a mover sus piezas. Džodić está en su radar y las conversaciones con su entorno confirman que el interés ha pasado a una fase más concreta. El verano todavía queda lejos, pero en el Metropolitano quieren anticiparse para intentar hacerse con uno de los futbolistas que consideran una inversión de futuro.

articles.title: Un golazo en memoria de su abuela
articles.standfirst: Luka Sucic marcó un gran tanto en San Mamés que dedicó al cielo entre lágrimas, en recuerdo de la madre de su padre, fallecida el sábado y con la que se crio
articles.summary: Luka Sucic marcó un gran tanto en San Mamés que dedicó al cielo entre lágrimas, en recuerdo de la madre de su padre, fallecida el sábado y con la que se crio
articles.body: Luka Sucic marcó en San Mamés su cuarto gol en lo que llevamos de una Liga en la que es el máximo realizador de la Real Sociedad, confirmando una vez más lo bien que ha empezado esta temporada, en la que después de dos decepcionantes se jugaba reivindicarse y ser un futbolista importante para los txuriurdin, algo que ha conseguido. El 24 rompió a llorar al dedicarlo al cielo, debido al fallecimiento el sábado de una abuela con la que guardaba muy buena y estrecha relación, ya que de niño pasó mucho tiempo con ella. Sucic, como el resto de sus compañeros, arrancó muy mal el derbi en Bilbao, con el Athletic adelantándose con justicia por sus claras ocasiones, pero a partir del 1-0 el croata fue uno de los txuriurdin que reaccionó bien, ya que desde la desventaja los de Matarazzo crecieron y fruto de ello llegó el gran zurdazo con el que el 24 logró el empate. El croata miró y señaló al cielo en la celebración e incluso se le escaparon algunas lágrimas, al acordarse se su abuela fallecida el sábado, un hecho que le causó una gran tristeza y por la que estuvo a punto de no jugar, aunque al final lo hizo pensando en rendirle el mejor homenaje y el golazo lo fue. Fue el cuarto tanto de Sucic en esta LaLiga, en la que es el máximo realizador de la Real y uno de los 20 primeros del campeonato, el sexto en esta temporada, en la que como hemos apuntado está sacando todo el alto nivel futbolistico que se le suponía y por el que la Real pagó 12 millones de euros que hasta hace unos meses parecían muchos, pero que ahora dan la sensación de estar muy bien invertidos. El atacante realista deberá descansar muy bien estos días, porque el jueves el equipo de Pellegrino Matarazzo disputa muy importante cuarta jornada de la Europa League, en Anoeta contra el Olympique de Lyon, dando un paso muy importante hacia el top 8 en caso de hacerse con los tres puntos.

articles.title: Paul Merson: Arsenal showed mark of champions against Liverpool in 'defensive masterclass' victory at Anfield
articles.summary: Paul Merson says Arsenal showed 'mark of champions' in 1-0 win at Liverpool, their first for 14 years, having denied Reds a single shot on target to move three points clear at top through Kai Havertz's winner
articles.body:
Kai Havertz's 16th-minute winner went on to prove enough to settle the game and give Arsenal a first win at Liverpool in 14 years and their fourth straight league win. In doing so, they became the first team to deny the Reds a single shot on target in a home league match since Opta records began in 2003.

Former Arsenal midfielder Merson had tipped the Gunners to get beaten at Anfield but believes Sunday's victory showed they have the mark of champions, dispelling any doubts of a drop-off following their shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton last month...

The way Arsenal defend, everyone does the right thing. When you're watching top, top players who have just won the league and still defend like they do, it's a masterclass.

They got away with a couple of things with the VAR and the pull back and things like that but bar that, credit where it's due. David Raya didn't really make a save.

You could call it a mark of champions. Let's not get away from the situation with Man City, but you just can't see anything but an Arsenal title. I said at the start of the season they'd win it by double digits and no doubt they will.

They haven't won at Liverpool in 13 years and they've just gone and done it. They got beaten by Brighton 3-0 and you wonder whether they've taken their foot off the pedal after winning the league.

'They've gone back to type since Brighton'

When they won it [the Premier League], I thought we'd see an Arsenal team which goes out and plays with a little bit more flair. They bought Bruno Guimaraes who's a good footballer and started well but then they go to Brighton and get destroyed - and I mean destroyed.

They probably have a meeting and think they need to go back to what won them everything. I thought they were outstanding in the first 20 minutes on Sunday, and if they'd got a second goal they would have won comfortably.

But after they didn't, they shut up shop and said to break them down. It should've been a penalty on Alexander Isak but for all the ball Liverpool had around the box, Raya never made a save.

They've gone back to type, they are an absolutely machine - at the highest level.

'Arteta must go to bed and think... wow'

They are top, top players and every player should look at this team. Every manager's dream would be this Arsenal team. Mikel Arteta must go to bed and think, 'wow'. Everything he tells them to do, they do it. You can't say that about Michael Carrick, can you?

I can't see anyone beating them to the league title. They'll win it comfortably.

They had the second half at Anfield completely under control. My one question in the Champions League is whether they have it in them to hurt you on the counter-attack. If Liverpool were 1-0 down to PSG yesterday, when PSG have their three up front you're thinking they'll pick the right pass on the counter and win it three or four.

Arsenal just haven't got that little bit of guile on the ball.

They don't have to score a lot of goals in the Premier League though, because this team is unbelievable to watch.

articles.title: Tensión y gran susto en el Heliodoro: terrible entrada de Owono a Jesús de Miguel
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Tenerife quedó tendido sobre el césped después de recibir un fuerte impacto en el pecho con la rodilla del portero del Andorra
articles.summary: El delantero del Tenerife quedó tendido sobre el césped después de recibir un fuerte impacto en el pecho con la rodilla del portero del Andorra
articles.body: El Tenerife-Andorra se convirtió en una auténtica pesadilla en el minuto 98. Cuando el encuentro ya había enloquecido tras el 2-2 y las expulsiones de Lautaro y Dani Martín, una acción inesperada terminó por helar el Heliodoro Rodríguez López. Jesús de Miguel quedó desplomado sobre el césped después de sufrir un durísimo impacto de Owono, que salió a toda velocidad de su área para intentar despejar un balón y acabó arrollando al delantero blanquiazul. El Tenerife buscaba una nueva oportunidad para adelantarse en el marcador. Recuperó la pelota y lanzó un contragolpe que permitió a Jesús de Miguel arrancar desde su propio campo en busca de un balón aéreo. El atacante ganó la carrera a los dos últimos defensores del Andorra y fijó su mirada en la pelota para intentar controlarla. No podía imaginar lo que se le venía encima. Owono, que había abandonado su área a toda velocidad para despejar el balón, impactó con la rodilla sobre el pecho del delantero blanquiazul. El choque fue brutal. De Miguel cayó inmediatamente al suelo, inmóvil, mientras los futbolistas de ambos equipos reclamaban asistencia médica con gestos de desesperación. El colegiado mostró la tarjeta roja al guardameta del Andorra, pero el partido había pasado a un segundo plano. Las escenas de pánico se sucedieron sobre el césped. Owono, que ya se retiraba del terreno de juego después de su expulsión, regresó para interesarse por el estado del atacante. Las asistencias médicas entraron rápidamente y atendieron a Jesús de Miguel durante más de cinco minutos, mientras el Heliodoro permanecía en un silencio sobrecogedor. El delantero fue finalmente trasladado en camilla hacia una ambulancia medicalizada situada en el exterior del estadio. Allí aguardaban, con evidentes muestras de preocupación, el presidente del Tenerife, Felipe Miñambres, el máximo accionista, Rayco García, y varios compañeros del futbolista. La angustia se prolongó durante aproximadamente un cuarto de hora. Finalmente, la ambulancia abandonó el estadio rumbo a un centro hospitalario, acompañada por los servicios médicos del conjunto isleño. El fútbol quedó completamente eclipsado por una acción que conmocionó a todos los presentes en el Heliodoro.

articles.title: El Andorra empata al Tenerife en la recta final en un partido con tres rojas y susto final
articles.standfirst: El encuentro se acaba un minuto antes por el tremendo choque de Owono y Jesús de Miguel que acaba con el delantero en camilla y trasladado a un hospital
articles.summary: Del 2-0 se pasó al 2-2. La tangana posterior al 2-1 acabó con las expulsiones de Lautaro y Dani Martín
articles.body: El Tenerife halló un oasis que terminó convertido en espejismo. Después de seis jornadas sin ganar, los blanquiazules parecían haber encontrado la salida del desierto con los goles de Christian Gomis y Enric Gallego. Sin embargo, el Andorra devolvió de golpe a la realidad a los blanquiazules en apenas seis minutos. Un penalti por mano de Viereck, transformado por Lautaro, y un cabezazo de Golubovic tras un centro de Spatz desde la derecha deshicieron la ventaja local y dejaron al Heliodoro sumido en la incredulidad. El partido, además, terminó con las expulsiones de Lautaro y Dani Martín, enfrentados en una pelea por alcanzar el balón después de que el argentino lo alojara en la red. Y con otra roja directa para Owono después de que el guardameta derribase violentamente a Jesús De Miguel en una disputa por un balón aéreo fuera del área que terminó con el blanquiazul conmocionado y evacuado tras ser atendido por las asistencias durante varios minutos sobre el césped. El primer acto había sido un ejercicio de pragmatismo y eficacia del Tenerife. Los blanquiazules no necesitaron más que una llegada para golpear. Gallego le robó la cartera a Schneider en tres cuartos de campo y lanzó a Christian Gomis, que ganó la carrera a los zagueros andorranos y batió a Owono en su salida. Un golpe certero que premió la voracidad local y castigó el primer desliz visitante. El Andorra asumió el mando conforme avanzaban los minutos y monopolizó la posesión con combinaciones cada vez más cerca del área de Dani Martín. En una de ellas, Domenech filtró un balón que Schneider convirtió en un disparo al larguero. El Heliodoro contuvo la respiración ante el aviso y el Tenerife respondió con una transición que cambió de nuevo el guion. Noel López recibió en la frontal, se citó con Martí Vilá y, con habilidad, se zafó de su marcador. El leve agarrón cuando se internaba en el área terminó en penalti. Enric Gallego, fiel a su cita con el gol ante su afición, asumió la responsabilidad y resolvió con un zurdazo raso a la izquierda de Owono. El Andorra pasó del posible 1-1 al 2-0 en cuestión de segundos. Un castigo demoledor para un equipo al que la fortuna le había dado la espalda. Pero el Tenerife perdió el norte en el epílogo cuando parecía haber saciado, por fin, su sed de triunfos. Viereck cometió una mano dentro del área que Lautaro convirtió desde los once metros para devolver al Andorra al partido. El Tenerife apenas tuvo tiempo de recomponerse antes de encajar el segundo. Spatz encontró espacio por la derecha y puso un balón que Golubovic cabeceó a la red. Seis minutos bastaron para dinamitar una ventaja que parecía sólida y transformar por completo el escenario del encuentro. La celebración del empate derivó en una pelea entre Lautaro y Dani Martín por hacerse con el balón después de que el argentino lo alojara en la red. El enfrentamiento terminó con ambos expulsados y añadió todavía más tensión a un partido que había cambiado por completo de dueño. El Tenerife, que había encontrado un oasis después de seis jornadas de sequía, se vio de nuevo atrapado en su propio desierto.

articles.title: Sporting Lisbon parts way with coach Rui Borges ahead of Champions League match
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Sporting Lisbon is parting ways with coach Rui Borges after the club's slow start to the season, with reserve-team coach Tiago Fernandes taking...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — Sporting Lisbon is parting ways with coach Rui Borges after the club's slow start to the season, with reserve-team coach Tiago Fernandes taking temporary control ahead of the Champions League match against Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Tuesday.

Sporting is third in the Portuguese league, already nine points behind leader Porto.

The club said in a statement Monday that it has begun discussions with Rui Borges "with a view to terminating his employment contract."

Tiago Fernandes will be in charge of the first team on an interim basis until Rui Borges' replacement is appointed, the Lisbon-based club added.

Lyon coach Paulo Fonseca is expected to take over, according to French media. Fonseca told reporters there was a possibility he could leave the Ligue 1 side after Lyon's 2-0 win against Angers on Sunday in Ligue 1.

In the Champions League, Sporting won its first two games — against Galatasaray and Lens — but surprisingly lost at home to LASK of Austria in the last round.

Borges took over at Sporting in December 2024 after leaving his role as Vitoria de Guimaraes coach. He replaced João Pereira , who lasted just six weeks as the successor to Ruben Amorim, and guided Sporting to a successful defense of its Portuguese league title.

Last season, Sporting also reached the quarterfinals of the Champions League, only losing to eventual runner-up Arsenal 1-0 on aggregate.

articles.title: UCLA moves up to No. 5 in the Associated Press college football poll
articles.summary: The UCLA Bruins took the No. 5 spot in both the Coaches Poll and in this week’s Associated Press Top-25 poll.
articles.body:
It has taken Bob Chesney less than one year to turn the UCLA Bruins into a top-five team in the country. UCLA took the No. 5 spot in both the Coaches Poll and in this week's Associated Press Top-25 poll .

UCLA is the surprise team in the nation, unexpectedly being 8-0 in Chesney's first year in Westwood. While it's unclear what UCLA's ceiling is this season with backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, UCLA has proven to have a very high floor under Chesney.

Bruin defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler has his unit playing exceptional football and UCLA has found enough success on offense to stack together the eight-straight victories but things are about to get tougher. UCLA got through the soft part of their schedule unscathed but road games against Minnesota and Michigan and home bouts with Illinois and USC could put the undefeated season in jeopardy.

Miami (FL) owns the No. 1 spot in the nation, ahead of Georgia, Utah, Notre Dame and UCLA in the top-five. USC is back in the top-25 after their big win over Ohio State, climbing up to No. 18. The Trojans is the only ranked team left on UCLA's schedule, with Minnesota having received votes but did not crack the Top-25.

Each week UCLA has climbed up the rankings, with Chesney and the team continuing to prove themselves by stacking win after win. With a strong end to the season, UCLA will find themselves with their first-ever College Football Playoff berth, with the regular season finale against USC potentially having a lot on the line for both programs.

articles.title: David Moyes sends a strong message! Jack Grealish left out AGAIN for Newcastle clash as Everton boss stands firm after training breach
articles.summary: Jack Grealish has been omitted from the Everton matchday squad for the second consecutive fixture as manager David Moyes continues to take a hardline stance...
articles.body:
Jack Grealish has been omitted from the Everton matchday squad for the second consecutive fixture as manager David Moyes continues to take a hardline stance on disciplinary standards at Goodison Park. The England international was noticeably absent from the group that travelled to face Newcastle United in the Premier League on Monday evening.

Disciplinary fallout continues for Grealish

Everton have taken the significant decision to leave Grealish at home for their vital Premier League encounter against Newcastle United. The 31-year-old winger, who is currently on a second season-long loan from Manchester City, has found himself in the middle of a disciplinary storm after failing to report for a scheduled training session last Monday. This latest exclusion follows his absence from the squad during the club's Carabao Cup victory over the same opponents last week, suggesting that the hierarchy is not yet ready to reintegrate the creative playmaker into the first-team fold.

While the club initially cited "illness" as the reason for his absence during a 2-0 loss to Arsenal on October 24, the situation escalated when he missed training without permission shortly thereafter. Reports suggest the England international has remained on Merseyside to focus on his individual conditioning at the club's Finch Farm base. Grealish had been a regular fixture in the starting XI prior to these incidents, having made four consecutive starts, but he now faces an uncertain road back into the squad as he works on building fitness away from the main group.

Toffees boss has been vocal in his support of the internal measures taken against the high-profile loanee. Speaking after the recent cup win, Moyes made it clear that the club's principles would not be compromised for any individual, regardless of their status or talent. "You probably know I'm not going to give any details, it is a club decision and I support that decision. It is something I don't want to speak too much about," Moyes explained to Daily Mail . The manager's firm stance highlights a desire to maintain a culture of accountability within a squad that he describes as having limited depth but high work ethic.

"The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it. All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job," the Scotsman added. He further noted the importance of humility within the camp, stating that they are not accepting any excuses as they strive to keep challenging for results despite having a relatively small squad.

The timing of Grealish's absence from training has coincided with reports regarding his activities during a recent break. Information has surfaced indicating that the winger was involved in two nights of partying and drinking in London and Wilmslow. These social excursions reportedly took place following the Pride of Britain awards, where he was seen at a karaoke bar and later a pub alongside several team-mates and former colleagues. While these reports have not been officially linked to his exclusion by the club, they have certainly added to the scrutiny surrounding his professional conduct during this loan spell.

Having rejoined Everton in the summer, Grealish has made seven appearances so far, but his momentum has been completely halted by this recent string of events. The Toffees are currently navigating a difficult period of the season, and the loss of a key creative asset like Grealish is a blow to their attacking options.

articles.title: Has India ever won a ODI series in New Zealand? IND vs NZ full head-to-head record, series results in One-day cricket listed
articles.summary: With India all set to face New Zealand in the 1st ODI, here's a look at their head-to-head record in away conditions and if India has ever won a series in NZ...
articles.body:
India have won two of the 10 ODI series they have played in New Zealand , in 2008/09 and 2018/19, and begin their 11th there on November 4.

India lead the overall ODI head-to-head 63-52 from 123 matches, with one tie and seven no results.

New Zealand lead 26-14 in matches played on their own soil, where India have never won more than four in a series.

India's ODI record in New Zealand ahead of the November 4 series opener

India begin a five-match ODI series at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday, November 4, having taken the T20I leg 3-2 and with two Tests to follow before the tour ends on December 1. The 50-over leg moves on to Wellington, Hamilton and then Bay Oval in Tauranga for the last two.

The recent record between the sides in this format belongs to New Zealand. They won 2-1 in India in January, their first ODI series victory on Indian soil, after India had won the Champions Trophy semi-final meeting in Dubai in March 2025.

New Zealand has long been the harder assignment of the two. India have toured for 10 ODI series there since 1975/76 and won two, drawing two and losing the other six, which makes it the fixture's most lopsided split.

Across all venues, India lead 63-52 from 123 matches, with the tie coming at Auckland in January 2014 and seven matches ending without a result. New Zealand have the edge at neutral venues as well, having won the 2000 ICC KnockOut final in Nairobi and their group meeting at the 1999, 1979 and 1975 World Cups among others.

India vs New Zealand overall ODI head-to-head record

India vs New Zealand ODI head-to-head record at home

In India, the two sides have met 43 times, with India winning 32 and New Zealand 10, a win rate above 74 per cent. One match, in Chennai in October 2003, was abandoned without a result.

India vs New Zealand ODI head-to-head record in India

India's biggest win in the fixture came at home, by 190 runs in Visakhapatnam on October 29, 2016. They also swept New Zealand 5-0 in India in 2010/11, winning in Guwahati, Jaipur, Vadodara, Bengaluru and Chennai.

New Zealand's 10 wins in India are spread thinly, and until this January they had never strung enough together to take a series there. They managed it in 2025/26, winning in Rajkot by seven wickets and Indore by 41 runs after losing the opener in Vadodara.

India vs New Zealand ODI head-to-head record away

New Zealand's home advantage in this fixture is substantial. They have won 26 of the 45 ODIs played there against India's 14, with one tie at Auckland in 2014 and four matches producing no result.

India vs New Zealand ODI head-to-head record in New Zealand

India's biggest win in New Zealand is by 90 runs, at Mount Maunganui on January 26, 2019, during their most successful tour there. New Zealand's heaviest home win over India came by 108 runs at Dunedin in March 1990.

The 2019 tour accounts for a good share of India's total. They won the first three at Napier and Mount Maunganui, lost the fourth in Hamilton by eight wickets and then took the fifth in Wellington by 35 runs for a 4-1 result.

Since then, India have not won an ODI in New Zealand. They lost all three in 2019/20 and then went down in Auckland in November 2022 before rain washed out the remaining two matches in Hamilton and Christchurch.

India and New Zealand have played 18 bilateral ODI series, of which India have won nine, New Zealand seven and two were drawn. India's record at home is 7-1, while in New Zealand they trail 6-2 with two draws.

India's two series wins in New Zealand came 10 years apart, 3-1 in 2008/09 and 4-1 in 2018/19. The 2008/09 result was India's first ever ODI series victory in the country, 33 years after they first toured.

The drawn series are worth noting too. India came from behind to level 2-2 in 1993/94 and did the same in 1998/99, where a washout in Wellington left the five-match series tied.

So the answer is yes, twice in 10 attempts, and not since Virat Kohli's side won there in early 2019. The series that begins in Auckland on November 4 will be India's 11th ODI tour of New Zealand and their sixth five-match series in the country.

articles.title: El árbitro suspende el partido de mutuo acuerdo entre todas las partes con 2 minutos por jugarse
articles.standfirst: Expulsó a Owono por "impactar bruscamente con su pierna en alto sobre un adversario con uso de fuerza excesiva"
articles.summary: Expulsó a Owono por "impactar bruscamente con su pierna en alto sobre un adversario con uso de fuerza excesiva"
articles.body: manuel Ángel Pérez Hernández, colegiado madrileño y encargado de arbitrar el Tenerife-Andorra, describió en el acta arbitral la tarjeta roja que mostró al guardameta Owono y que provocó el desplome de Jesús de Miguel. "Fue expulsado por impactar bruscamente con su pierna en alto sobre un adversario con uso de fuerza excesiva cuando el balón estaba en disputa. El jugador fue atendido sobre el terreno de juego, abandonando posteriormente el campo en camilla". Sobre la suspensión del partido el árbitro escribió en el acta lo siguiente: "El partido fue detenido en el minuto 96 para la atención médica del jugador dorsal 9 del equipo local. Ante la gravedad de los hechos y no observando mejoría sobre el estado de salud de dicho jugador, nos retiramos a vestuarios. Una vez reunidos con capitanes y delegados de ambos equipos, nos comunican que no se encuentran en disposición anímica de continuar el partido. Por lo tanto se decide dar por suspendido el partido tras el mutuo acuerdo por todas las partes". En el momento de la suspensión del partido y tomando como referencia la visión desde la zona de banquillos, el C.D Tenerife se encontraba a la izquierda del terreno de juego y el F.C Andorra se encontrada a la derecha, el resultado del partido es de C.D Tenerife (2)- F.C Andorra (2), la reanudación sería mediante un tiro libre directo en el centro del campo favorable al CD Tenerife y restaban 2 minutos por jugarse. articles.title: Donyell Malen at Roma: Man Utd face the top scorer in Europe’s major leagues in 2026 with the Dutchman transformed
articles.summary: Donyell Malen has been on fire in front of goal for Roma since signing from Aston Villa and that makes him the last man Manchester United want to face in the Champions League. Adam Bate examines the transformation of the Netherlands international in Italy
articles.body:
Malen was a popular figure at Aston Villa but even his biggest admirers might not have anticipated all this. Fourteen goals in 18 Serie A games on loan last season certainly suggested that Roma could get the best from him but Malen has gone to another level.

He began with a hat-trick against Fiorentina and now has eight goals in eight Serie A games. There was a suspension for a red card in there too but it hardly stopped him. He goes to Old Trafford on the back of goals against Cagliari and Udinese in the past week.

In 2026, Malen has scored 18 goals from open play, two more than nearest rival Lamine Yamal and four more than anyone else in the big leagues. Just an Italian thing? Not quite. In the Champions League, Malen bagged a brace against Real Madrid last month.

The obvious question is how and why this is happening. Now 27, Malen felt like a known quantity in European football. It is over a decade ago that he was a youngster at Arsenal. Speaking to him last year about those early days, he explained: "I was this skinny [kid]."

He was honest enough to admit that it all came too soon for him. "I was only 16 when I trained with the first team. Maybe I was not really 100 per cent ready. Looking back, I learnt a lot in those two and a half years there. But I made my steps in a different way."

At PSV, he was prolific. But his big move to Borussia Dortmund saw him deliver only sporadically. Malen certainly had his moments but nothing sustained like this and he was perhaps a victim of his ability to play in various different positions across the front line.

Speaking to Unai Emery at the time of his arrival at Villa, that versatility was part of the appeal. "We are practising with him in different positions, attacking third, sometimes right side, which is a little bit of a priority, but as well as a No 10 and as a striker."

Malen offered the usual spiel about being relaxed about his role. "I have played all the positions by now at this stage, so for me it does not really matter." But there was one line when talking to him that betrayed his true feelings. "I just want to be close to the goal."

Emery knew this, of course. "He likes to be close in the opponent's goal and he likes to score goals." But Villa had Ollie Watkins up front. It has taken Gian Piero Gasperini to bring out the best in Malen over an extended period. He has done so by unleashing him up top.

"He wanted to be a centre-forward, and I always thought that is where he was stronger too because he is deadly near the penalty area." The experienced Roma coach did add an important caveat. "Admittedly, I did not expect his numbers to be so astonishing."

There have been the familiar power finishes but two of his goals past David de Gea in the Fiorentina game were with his left foot. At Lecce, there was a delightful dink. There have been poached efforts and examples of him showcasing his prodigious speed from deep.

It is easy to recognise it now but Gasperini's style of play seems ideally suited to a player with Malen's skill-set. The man-to-man approach emphasises his quality in one-on-one situations, where his pace and dribbling ability makes him a match for anyone.

Once in behind the defence, which happens often with Gasperini's vertical game, there is no catching him either. "Running in behind, trying to create space for midfielders. I think that is my strength." No one in Serie A has had more touches in the opposition box.

Can Manchester United stop him? The recent record of their sluggish and sloppy defence suggests that Malen could be their worst nightmare. He makes the trip to Old Trafford as a different proposition to the player last seen on these shores in January.

With his coach likening him to the late great Gianluca Vialli because of his "similar ability to shake off his marker and get in behind" defences, this is a different Donyell Malen. One boasting a scoring record that shows he is the deadliest striker in Europe right now.

articles.title: England to host South Africa in three-Test netball series live on Sky Sports in February as World Cup preparation
articles.summary: Vitality Roses will tackle the Proteas twice in London and once in Leicester in February 2027; games will help sides prepare for Netball World Cup in Australia in August and September; England edged South Africa this summer to reach Commonwealth Games semi-finals at opponents' expense
articles.body:
The games will serve as preparation for the 2027 World Cup in Australia across late August and early September.

England, currently third in the world rankings, will take on fifth-placed South Africa at Wembley Arena in London on February 6 and 7 before the series concludes at Leicester's Mattioli Arena on February 10.

The Vitality Roses edged the Proteas 58-54 in their final pool game of this summer's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow to reach the semi-finals at their opponents' expense.

South Africa had beaten England 2-1 in the sides' previous Test series in January 2026, winning the deciding match 65-50 in Johannesburg.

Before playing the Proteas early next year, England will face Jamaica home and away in the autumn.

Fran Connolly, the chief executive of England Netball said: "This international series against South Africa forms an important part of our preparations ahead of the Netball World Cup.

"We now have two opportunities to test ourselves against world-class nations, including fixtures at home and away, that will put us in the best position possible heading into the summer.

"We're looking forward to welcoming South Africa and feeling the support of a home crowd behind us."

Mami Diale, the president of Netball South Africa added: "Playing the Vitality Roses at a time like this is very important for us - this allows us to gauge our state of readiness ahead of the World Cup.

"We have faced England a few times recently and it is always a spectacle.

"Playing teams that are ranked in the top five is very important because it allows us an opportunity to measure in terms of how far we are, what we need to work on and what we are doing right."

Saturday February 6 (Wembley Arena, London)

Sunday February 7 (Wembley Arena, London)

Wednesday February 10 (Mattioli Arena, Leicester)

articles.title: Bill Belichick Responds to Jordon Hudson Breakup Rumors Amid Speculation on Dating Status
articles.summary: North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick was not forthcoming on Monday when questioned about the rumors of his potential breakup with Jordon Hudson.
articles.body:
North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick was not forthcoming on Monday when questioned about the rumors of his potential breakup with Jordon Hudson.

"Do you work for a tabloid now?" he told reporters . "I'll keep my personal comments and relationships to myself if that's alright with you."

The relationship between Belichick, 74, and Hudson, 25, became something of a national fascination in 2025. In March of that year, reports emerged that Belichick requested Hudson to be copied on any email correspondence sent to him from the school.

One month later, when the head coach was asked about his relationship with Hudson during an interview on CBS Mornings , she shut down those questions while sitting off to the side.

Her proximity to the North Carolina football program invited scrutiny, to the point that podcast host and journalist Pablo Torre reported claims that Hudson had been banned from the football facilities. North Carolina denied that reporting.

In the meantime, Belichick has gone 8-12 in parts of two seasons as UNC's head football coach. This year's team is currently 4-4 and mired in a two-game losing streak after Saturday's 38-35 loss against top-ranked Miami.

articles.summary: Su ampliación de contrato está ahora mismo parada y se compromete con MRH Football Agency
articles.body: Rafita se ha consolidado como uno de los jugadores más destacados del Málaga en este inicio de temporada. El lateral axárquico ha sido una de las revelaciones del equipo durante las 11 primeras jornadas de LaLiga EA Sports y su rendimiento también le permitió entrar en la última convocatoria de la selección española sub-21. Con el combinado nacional disputó dos encuentros como titular, dejando buenas sensaciones y acumulando una importante carga de minutos. El futbolista tiene contrato con el Málaga hasta 2029, aunque la entidad llevaba tiempo trabajando en una mejora de sus condiciones. La intención del club pasaba por revisar su vinculación y elevar, entre otros aspectos, la cláusula de rescisión que figura actualmente en su contrato. Sin embargo, según ha podido saber Radio MARCA Málaga, las negociaciones han quedado paralizadas en las últimas semanas después de que Rafita haya cambiado de representación. El futbolista ha pasado a formar parte de MRH Football Agency, que este lunes anunció oficialmente su incorporación a través de sus redes sociales. El cambio de agencia no ha modificado la postura del Málaga, que mantiene su intención de mejorar el contrato del lateral. MRH Football Agency ya representa a otros futbolistas de la actual plantilla blanquiazul, entre ellos Chupete y Fernando Calero. articles.body: El apellido Pérez vuelve a ilusionar a todo el país y, en especial, a la hinchada de Independiente Santa Fe. La Federación Colombiana de Fútbol anunció de manera oficial la lista de convocados para el nuevo microciclo de trabajo de la Selección Colombia Masculina Sub-19, bajo la dirección técnica de César Torres. La gran sorpresa y el centro de todas las miradas es el llamado de Franco Pérez, hijo del histórico y recordado ídolo cardenal Omar Sebastián Pérez. El joven mediocampo zurdo, quien actualmente se forma en las divisiones menores de Boca Juniors de Argentina, da así su primer paso oficial defendiendo los colores de la Tricolor, abriendo un nuevo capítulo para su carrera internacional. Franco Pérez, de 18 años, venía sonando con fuerza en el radar del combinado nacional gracias a su destacada evolución en el fútbol argentino, donde incluso firmó un vínculo contractual a largo plazo con el cuadro Xeneize. Con una estatura destacada de 1,90 metros y una gran visión de juego como volante zurdo, sus características físicas y técnicas llamaron inmediatamente la atención del cuerpo técnico juvenil de la FCF. Aunque su hermano Thiago eligió representar recientemente a las selecciones juveniles de Argentina, Franco se decantó por la Tricolor, cumpliendo el sueño de sumar sus primeros minutos y entrenamientos oficiales en el proceso de selecciones Colombia juveniles. El estratega César Torres convocó a un grupo selecto de jóvenes talentos del rentado nacional e internacional para este nuevo ciclo de preparación. Junto a Franco Pérez, la lista oficial incluye a los siguientes jugadores: Alam García – Independiente Yumbo Andrés Marín – Atlético Nacional Camilo Amú – América de Cali Christian Negrete – Real Cundinamarca Este proceso apunta a consolidar la base de cara a los próximos retos del balompié sudamericano y mundial en las categorías de formación, donde la gran promesa de la familia Pérez espera ganarse un lugar fijo y replicar la huella imborrable que dejó su padre en el corazón de los aficionados colombianos.

articles.title: El CTA reconoce un error en el chip del balón: "La explicación más probable es un ligero desfase..."
articles.standfirst: El Comité Técnico de Árbitros emite un comunicado y pide un informe a Kinexon
articles.summary: El Comité Técnico de Árbitros emite un comunicado y pide un informe a Kinexon
articles.body: el penalti señalado por Hernández Hernández de Aramburu a Nico Williams y que transformó Berenguer para decidir el Athletic-Real Sociedad se sigue analizando... porque da para ello. Tanto que el CTA ha emitido un comunicado para reconocer que hubo un error de sincronización del chip en ese balón tocado por el defensa venezolano. También ha informado que ha solicitado un informe a Kinexon, la empresa responsable. Mientras, el CTA defiende la labor del VAR, que, al fallar el chip, entendió que Aramburu no tocaba el balón y el penalti pitado por Hernández Hernández, el árbitro de campo, se lanzó. El Comité Técnico de Árbitros ha solicitado un informe a Kinexon, empresa responsable del desarrollo del Connected Ball (balón conectado), con el objetivo de esclarecer lo sucedido durante el encuentro disputado el pasado domingo en San Mamés entre el Athletic Club y la Real Sociedad, correspondiente a la jornada 11 de Primera División, en relación con la acción de penalti que dio lugar al segundo gol del conjunto local. Antes del encuentro, el árbitro VAR designado, que cuenta con una amplia experiencia en el uso de esta tecnología tras haberla utilizado en el pasado Mundial y haber recibido formación específica sobre su funcionamiento (fue el único árbitro VAR español que acudió al Mundial), realizó con el operador de VAR antes del encuentro la sincronización prevista en el protocolo, sin que se detectara incidencia alguna. Asimismo, Mediapro efectuó durante el partido comprobaciones aleatorias de dicha sincronización. En una acción del primer tiempo, el árbitro señaló penalti al considerar punible el derribo de un defensor de la Real Sociedad sobre un atacante del Athletic Club. La jugada fue revisada desde la sala VOR y, conforme a la visualización disponible en ese momento de la señal proporcionada por el Connected Ball, se interpretó que era el jugador del Athletic Club quien tocaba el balón, sin que lo tocase el jugador de la Real Sociedad. Al trasladarse posteriormente la métrica a la producción televisiva para mayor transparencia, se corroboró que el contacto del jugador del Athletic Club coincidía con el último pico registrado en la métrica (antes de que hipotéticamente el jugador de la Real Sociedad pudiese haber tocado el balón), sin que apareciese ningún otro con posterioridad, lo que indicaba que el futbolista de la Real Sociedad no había llegado a tocar el balón. No obstante, se apreciaron dos picos anteriores cuya correspondencia con las imágenes no resultaba clara. Ante esta circunstancia, el CTA solicitó a Kinexon un análisis específico de lo sucedido y una explicación detallada de esos dos picos previos al que, a priori, correspondía al último contacto del jugador del Athletic Club. El informe emitido por la compañía concluye: "La explicación más probable es un ligero desfase de sincronización de aproximadamente 1–2 fotogramas (20–40 milisegundos, a 50 fotogramas por segundo) entre la señal del balón y el vídeo del VAR. En la visualización original, los picos de la señal aparecen ligeramente antes que los contactos físicos correspondientes que se ven en el vídeo. Esto pudo llevar a interpretar que el jugador de la Real Sociedad no tocó el balón, ya que en el momento aparente del contacto no se veía ningún pico adicional. Sin embargo, al resincronizar la señal con el vídeo descontando este desfase, la señal encaja con lo que se ve en pantalla, no solo en esta acción sino también en lo que ocurre antes y después, algo que no sucedía en la visualización original. El pico más destacado coincide entonces con la llegada del jugador de la Real Sociedad al balón". A la vista de las conclusiones del informe, el jugador de la Real sí habría tocado en último lugar el balón pudiendo no ser correcta la decisión de señalar penalti. Sin embargo, atendiendo exclusivamente a la información que el árbitro VAR tenía disponible en el momento de la revisión y a la sincronización que mostraba entonces el sistema, la resolución adoptada desde la sala VOR fue la correcta en dicho momento, al no disponer de evidencias que permitiesen modificar la decisión tomada sobre el terreno de juego y, precisamente, contar con una evidencia sólida (la métrica del balón conectado) que permitía aseverar que solo el jugador del Athletic Club había tocado el balón. El CTA considera igualmente relevante precisar que el Connected Ball funcionó correctamente durante el encuentro. La incidencia detectada se circunscribe al desfase de sincronización descrito entre la señal proporcionada por el balón y el vídeo utilizado por el VAR. El sensor del Kinexon Connected Ball proporciona información temporal de gran precisión. En su aplicación al VAR mediante cámaras de televisión, la señal del balón se sincroniza manualmente, por parte del operador de VAR, con el vídeo antes de cada encuentro mediante botes controlados del balón. Este procedimiento es diferente al empleado en el sistema de fuera de juego semiautomático (SAOT), en el que el Connected Ball y las cámaras específicas de seguimiento se sincronizan de manera continua mediante Precision Time Protocol (PTP), con precisión de milisegundos y sin necesidad de alineación manual. El Comité Técnico de Árbitros, aun tratándose de una incidencia técnica ajena al propio Comité, continuará colaborando con las empresas y profesionales responsables de estas tecnologías para perfeccionar los procedimientos de utilización y sincronización, reforzar su fiabilidad y minimizar la posibilidad de que situaciones de esta naturaleza puedan repetirse. El objetivo del CTA es que la incorporación de herramientas tecnológicas al arbitraje se produzca con las máximas garantías y contribuya a facilitar la labor arbitral y a mejorar la precisión y fiabilidad de las decisiones.

articles.title: Newcastle 0-1 Everton: Toffees earn first away league win of season as Magpies booed off after Jacob Ramsey sees red
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Everton earn first away league win of season with 1-0 victory at sorry Newcastle; home side booed off as Thierno Barry's winner inflicted back-to-back home defeats; Newcastle substitute Jacob Ramsey sent off in stoppage time for two yellows in 86 seconds
articles.body:
Newcastle's miserable evening deepened in stoppage time as substitute Jacob Ramsey was sent off after picking up two bookings in just 86 seconds.

The disappointing Magpies were beaten by Everton for a second time in the space of four days after their 3-1 Carabao Cup fourth-round defeat on Merseyside.

Another sorry display from Matthias Jaissle's side was underlined by Barry's 49th-minute winner, which Sky Sports commentator Andy Hinchcliffe labelled as "truly shocking" defending and "terrible goalkeeping".

Newcastle reacted slowly to Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's quick free-kick, which released Tyrique George, whose shot somehow squirmed under Lukas Hornicek, allowing Barry to tap home into an empty net.

Toon boss Jaissle, however, believed the goal should have "clearly" been disallowed for a stray elbow from Barry on Fabian Schar in the build-up.

Everton, who were once again without Jack Grealish, should have been ahead earlier in the game as Barry and Harrison Armstrong wasted great first-half chances, with Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher calling Newcastle "poor".

Anthony Elanga came closest to equalising for Newcastle as he hit the post in the 66th minute.

It took the home side until the 85th minute to register their first shot on target through substitute Yoane Wissa, who five minutes later forced a good save from ex-Sunderland goalkeeper Jordan Pickford.

Ramsey's 98th-minute red card helped Everton to hold on as they inflicted back-to-back home defeats on Newcastle, who have now lost four of their last five games in all competitions.

But for Everton, their first away league success since victory at St James' Park in February, moves David Moyes' side up to seventh, while Newcastle fall to 13th.

Carra: Boring Newcastle in for a tough season

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher speaking on Monday Night Football :

"Watching them of late, especially at home, it feels flat and a little bit boring, and that was one thing I didn't think I'd ever be describing Jaissle's Newcastle as.

"You think of the system he's come from, the Red Bull model, how they like to play. At times, those types of teams and managers can leave themselves open at the back, but it's front-footed, it's aggressive, it's getting the crowd involved, and we've just never seen any of that at all tonight [Monday] really. And that's the one where I'm a little bit sort of flummoxed watching it.

"I think it's going to be a tough season for Newcastle. They've got a lot of young players, they've got a young manager in there. The crowd are expecting a lot more."

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking to Sky Sports on the boos:

"After a performance like that, I can understand that. That's a reality, and I am responsible for that.

"We need to work again and again on the things we need to improve. After today, that's a lot."

On the loss: "We had a different approach. It looked so good during the week; I have to say the lads were committed to what we were doing, and today we can just look back and wonder why we couldn't bring it on the pitch. If you can't deliver when it counts, you don't deserve to win.

"We were not brave enough in possession. Too many long balls.

"It feels at the moment that there's not too much confidence. Not only with the young lads, but also with the more experienced ones. We have to overcome that as a unit. It is expected when you are in transition. Only together can we come out of it."

Everton boss David Moyes speaking to Sky Sports :

"I'm incredibly proud of the team all the time because their effort and their commitment are unquestionable.

"The way they go about their work is terrific. There's not a lot of them, but they are doing a great job at the moment.

"We're creating chances. That's the big thing for me. We want to be a side that creates more chances. If we could be more offensive, that's the way I'd like it to be. Thierno's had some big opportunities, and we need him to finish. He was on the spot today.

"I don't think anybody enjoys playing the same team twice so quickly. For us, winning in the League Cup and then coming to win in the league is hugely important. The points are important. We want to get back and nearer the top end of the league. It's incredibly tight."

24: HUGE MISS! Thierno Barry misses a "golden chance" according to Sky co-commentator Andy Hinchcliffe. He takes a wild swipe and completely misses the ball.

45+3: HUGE CHANCE! An unmarked Harrison Armstrong steers his first-time effort wide from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's pullback.

HALF-TIME! No shots on target for either side, with Newcastle booed off at the break.

49: EVERTON GOAL! A quick free-kick sees Tyrique George released and his shot squirms under Lukas Hornicek to allow Barry to rebound home.

66: NEWCASTLE CHANCE! Anthony Elanga tries to squeeze the ball home at the back stick but his ball hits the post and spins across the line as Everton clear.

90: PICKFORD SAVES! Yoane Wissa's first-time finish is well saved by Jordan Pickford with his outstretched leg.

90+8: RED CARD! Newcastle substitute Jacob Ramsey is sent off for a second yellow in the space of just 86 seconds.

Jack Grealish was not named in Everton's squad for the game at Newcastle, with the club citing a fitness issue.

The 31-year-old was left out of the team for Thursday's Carabao Cup fourth-round win over the Magpies due to a breach of club discipline after missing training.

Grealish was again left out at St James' Park, with a starting line-up post on the Everton club website stating that he was "not match fit".

After the win at Newcastle, Moyes said he "did not know yet" whether Grealish would be available for Friday's home Premier League game against Coventry, live on Sky Sports .

Asked whether there was a way back for Grealish, Moyes replied: "Of course there is."

articles.summary: Jugó 24 minutos tras lesionarse el pasado 20 de septiembre acortando casi dos semanas en su recuperación
articles.body: Aubameyang jugó 24 minutos tras estar cinco semanas recuperándose de una operación de menisco. articles.title: 'Newcastle are flat and boring' – Jamie Carragher warns Magpies face tough Premier League season after Everton defeat
articles.summary: Newcastle were booed off at home after losing 1-0 to Everton on Monday Night Football; Matthias Jaissle's side have lost three of their last four Premier League matches; Newcastle are 13th with three wins from nine games and head to Fulham, who are below them, on Saturday
articles.body:
Thierno Barry's second-half goal earned Everton a 1-0 win at St James' Park and their first away victory in the Premier League this season, as Newcastle were booed off at half-time and full-time following their fourth defeat in five games across all competitions.

Newcastle have slipped to 13th and are now four points above the bottom three, with a trip to lowly Fulham to come on Saturday.

"I think it is going to be a tough season for them," said Sky Sports' Carragher. "I felt tonight was actually more important for Newcastle than the cup game [Carabao Cup loss at Everton last week], and it was the other way round for Everton, who are desperate for a trophy.

"But I fear a little bit for Newcastle, I think it could be a long, tough season."

Jaissle was appointed in August, replacing Eddie Howe, and made a promising start by earning entertaining draws against Liverpool and Bournemouth, with a win at Tottenham sandwiched in between, but that has quickly faded as their home form has continued to be an issue.

No Premier League side has lost more home games in 2026 than Newcastle (7) and they have failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last 14 games at St James' Park, the longest run in their league history.

Carragher added: "Watching them of late, especially at home, it feels flat and a little bit boring, and that was one thing I didn't think I'd ever be describing Jaissle's Newcastle as.

"You think of the system he's come from, the Red Bull model, how they like to play. At times, those types of teams and managers can leave themselves open at the back, but it's front-footed, it's aggressive, it's getting the crowd involved, and we've just never seen any of that at all tonight [Monday]. I'm a little bit flummoxed watching it.

"I was really impressed with him, how he came across. They were very impressive at Spurs, a great result for them early on, and the results in the main have been okay, but I think there's always been a worry about the performances and their underlying numbers, even early on.

"I watched Fulham at Villa over the weekend, they were really good, and that'll be a tough game, and you look at some of the games they've got coming.

"I think it's going to be a tough season for Newcastle. They've got a lot of young players, they've got a young manager in there. The crowd are expecting a lot more."

Jaissle: Our plan didn't work - I understand boos

Jaissle opted for a different approach from their defeat against Everton four days earlier, but his tactical changes failed to pay off, with Newcastle not managing a shot on target until the 85th minute.

"Unfortunately we couldn't deliver our style of play across the whole 90 minutes," Jaissle told Sky Sports .

"That's something we are frustrated about. We had a different approach. It looked so good during the week, I have to say the lads were committed to what we were doing and today we can just look back and wonder why we couldn't bring it on the pitch. If you can't deliver when it counts, you don't deserve to win.

"We were not brave enough in possession. Too many long balls. We did not use our double six in possession where I think we were quite good against Everton a couple days ago. Then it was more of a wide game, back and forth, collecting second balls. That's something that we wanted to avoid to be more dominant.

"It feels at the moment that there's not too much confidence. Not only with the young lads, but also with the more experienced ones. We have to overcome that as a unit. It is expected when you are in transition. Only together we can come out of it.

"After a performance like that, I can understand that [fans booing]. That's a reality and I am responsible for that. We need to work again and again on the things we need to improve. After today, that's a lot."
